tasks.short: Coordinate departmental production, pricing, sales and distribution decisions.

steps.what: Review demand, capacity, stock, margins and delivery exceptions.
Discuss departmental constraints, customer commitments and emerging operational problems.
Compare volume, price, capacity and distribution options.
Agree trade-offs and approve departmental priorities within delegated authority.
Send approved priorities, owners and deadlines to department heads.
Request progress updates and chase overdue departmental actions.

tasks.design: Configure a {BI} exception view over {ERP}, {CRM} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, with deterministic scenario calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. The manager approves structured priorities in {WORKFLOW}, which creates {PROJECT} actions and sends internal reminders through {CHAT}; department heads execute commercial and operational changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Departmental plans use different assumptions, and decisions disappear into meetings and messages. Cross-functional authority cannot be reduced to a routing rule.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing dashboards and work-management features cover visibility and follow-up. Small calculation services can expose trade-offs without an autonomous agent.
tasks.still_hard: Demand is uncertain, departmental incentives conflict and customer commitments can outweigh calculated margins. Scenario quality depends on explicit assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: Secure commitments across department heads and accept responsibility for service, margin and capacity trade-offs.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly decisions on cross-department capacity bottlenecks.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time requesting updates and more time resolving bottlenecks with department heads. Cross-department decisions remain within the existing delegation framework.

reach.task: Propose a company-wide choice between growth, margin and service resilience.
reach.learn: Translate operating scenarios into strategic choices and explicit risk appetite.

evidence.claim: Existing reporting tools support dashboard summaries and questions about operational data.
Scenario arithmetic, action creation and reminders can use deterministic rules; cross-department trade-offs remain managerial.
Configuring existing reporting and work-management features is a plausible starting point, subject to installed capabilities.

assumptions: Department heads manage execution and bring cross-department conflicts to the general manager.
Existing {BI} and {PROJECT} capabilities can support exception views and action tracking.
Scenario calculations use declared assumptions rather than inferred customer behaviour.
Approved priorities are entered as structured decisions, avoiding a model transcription step.
Time and build estimates cover an initial business-unit rollout, not company-wide planning replacement.
unknowns: Which pricing, capacity and service decisions can the manager approve?
Are demand, capacity and margin measures comparable across departments?
Which systems already support action ownership and reminders?
Would proposed data use introduce employee monitoring requiring consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Which operating constraints can be expressed as auditable scenario rules?
Which exception thresholds reliably surface matters needing cross-department intervention?
new_work: Maintain scenario assumptions and exception thresholds.
Keep action owners and escalation routes current.
Review stale data and unresolved departmental dependencies.
Check that reminders support follow-up without creating duplicate reporting.
tasks.statement: Direct and coordinate activities of businesses or departments concerned with the production, pricing, sales, or distribution of products.

tasks.short: Help customers and support shelf replenishment and inventory checks during occasional sales-floor work.

steps.what: Greet customers and establish what help they need.
Look up product details, availability and stock location when needed.
Explain options, locate goods and help the customer choose.
Move available goods to shelves and check presentation.
Count goods at selected shelf and storage locations.
Enter counts and flag discrepancies for inventory review.

tasks.design: Configure a mobile lookup and count screen in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, using product information from the {ECOMMERCE} where needed. Capture counts once, calculate discrepancies and route them through the {WORKFLOW} to the inventory controller. Customer assistance, physical counting and replenishment remain human work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shared terminals interrupt customer conversations, and physical counts may need separate entry. Much of the task involves physical action that software cannot remove.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing mobile screens and barcode capture can reduce lookup and recording effort. A small integration may connect product details without requiring a model.
tasks.still_hard: Misplaced goods, inaccurate stock records, customer needs and shelf presentation require observation and physical action.
tasks.human_edge: Read customer cues, explain choices clearly and notice operational problems during direct floor contact.
tasks.altitude: The manager gains a little uninterrupted floor time through faster lookup and count capture. The role and decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Evaluate service standards through direct customer observation.
reach.learn: Turn repeated floor observations into service priorities while distinguishing patterns from isolated anecdotes.

evidence.claim: Mobile product lookup, barcode count capture and discrepancy routing are established deterministic patterns.
The digest supplies no documented case showing that software replaces the physical or interpersonal work described here.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to retail or customer-facing sites.
A general manager covers busy periods or observes operations; routine floor supervision belongs to site supervisors.
The workflow covers related floor activities, not a mandatory sequence for every customer.
Count records are observations; stock adjustments require the inventory controller's separate approval.
Build ranges assume existing mobile-compatible systems and devices; national consultation applies if working arrangements change.
unknowns: Whether existing devices and licences already support lookup and count capture.
Whether product information and store stock are consistently linked.
Frequency and duration of the manager's actual floor work.
Inventory adjustment approval rules and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Does lookup delay or inaccurate stock cause more customer interruption?
Can existing mobile configuration remove duplicate count entry without custom development?
new_work: Maintain product and location mappings.
Resolve synchronisation failures and duplicate counts.
Review discrepancies before authorising stock adjustments.
Keep mobile screens and shared-device access usable.
tasks.statement: Perform sales floor work, such as greeting or assisting customers, stocking shelves, or taking inventory.

tasks.short: Set marketing priorities, approve campaigns, coordinate delivery and decide what to change.

steps.what: Gather sales, campaign results and customer feedback.
Combine exports and reconcile campaign spending with sales.
Discuss customer needs, positioning and commercial priorities with department leads.
Draft the marketing plan, campaign briefs and proposed budget.

loop.input: Marketing choices, campaign scorecard, brand guidance and plan template.
loop.output: Draft marketing plan and campaign brief with linked evidence.
loop.check: Validate every figure against the scorecard; flag unsupported claims and missing decisions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved claims stay flagged for the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill budgets and dates, but positioning and campaign rationale require contextual writing.

steps.what: Approve campaign objectives, spending and commercial terms.
Brief marketing and sales leads and resolve delivery dependencies.
Check campaign settings and release approved advertising or promotions.
Prepare a campaign performance summary.

loop.input: Campaign scorecard, agreed objectives and campaign changes.
loop.output: Performance summary separating measured results from possible explanations.
loop.check: Check figures and periods automatically; prohibit unsupported causal claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; return unresolved discrepancies without a narrative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic; explaining mixed results needs bounded contextual writing.

steps.what: Decide whether to stop, adjust or extend the campaign.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins campaign, sales and spending data from the {ADS}, {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, {CRM} and {ERP}, feeding a checked {BI} scorecard. A template generator with bounded drafting loops prepares plans and reviews in the {DOCS}; the {WORKFLOW} records budget approval and the marketing lead's release approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Campaign identifiers, spending and sales were inconsistent across systems. Strategy also depended on customer context that templates could not capture.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and APIs support repeatable reconciliation. AI coding can reduce implementation effort, while bounded drafting helps turn approved choices into usable briefs.
tasks.still_hard: Attribution, brand judgement and commercial trade-offs remain difficult. Audience use must meet GDPR requirements; EU AI Act obligations depend on the intended model use.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a credible position, recognise customer concerns and accept responsibility for spending and public claims.

ambition.what: A fortnightly campaign stop-or-scale decision using reconciled contribution and pipeline evidence.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling plans and more time discussing customer response and delivery capacity. Within an agreed budget envelope, they can gain authority to move spending between approved campaigns.

reach.task: Choose which customer segment deserves additional investment.
reach.learn: Segment economics, contribution margins and how to distinguish experimental evidence from attribution.

evidence.claim: Report summarisation and data questions are supported today; reliable results depend on prepared data models.
Campaign reconciliation, approval routing and scheduled release can use deterministic integrations and configuration.
The digest provides no documented case proving improved marketing strategy or these estimated time reductions.

assumptions: Shares describe an illustrative campaign cycle, including delegated release work; they are not measured customer timings.
The manager works through marketing and sales leads rather than producing every campaign asset.
Build ranges cover one business unit and existing campaign channels.
Access estimates assume a known GDPR basis for audience data; any required consultation follows national rules.
unknowns: Whether campaign identifiers connect spending, leads and sales reliably.
Which existing systems support approval and scheduled release.
The manager's spending authority and the marketing lead's release authority.
Audience permissions, retention rules and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which campaign comparisons remain useful when sales attribution is incomplete?
How often do generated briefs introduce unsupported positioning or causal claims?
new_work: Resolve unmatched campaign costs and inconsistent identifiers.
Review generated briefs, public claims and performance explanations.
Maintain budget limits, audience checks, templates and integration credentials.
Record campaign changes so later comparisons remain interpretable.
tasks.statement: Develop or implement product-marketing strategies, including advertising campaigns or sales promotions.

tasks.short: Direct support departments, resolve competing priorities and hold department leads accountable for delivery.

steps.what: Review department spending, workload and service measures.
Read department reports and identify issues requiring discussion.

loop.input: Department reports, checked scorecard and previous decisions.
loop.output: Source-linked issues, unresolved commitments and proposed agenda.
loop.check: Require a source for each issue; validate numbers and preserve conflicting accounts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per report; flag unreadable or contradictory material.
loop.why_not_simpler: Department reports describe risks and dependencies in varied free text.

steps.what: Discuss delivery problems and coach department leads.
Resolve resource conflicts and approve changes in priorities.
Write decisions, expectations and instructions for department leads.
Assign department actions, owners and deadlines.
Chase action updates and consolidate status replies.
Handle escalations requiring cross-department intervention.

tasks.design: Configure shared department scorecards in the {BI} and action records in the {PROJECT}, with overdue exceptions replacing routine status chasing. A bounded reading loop prepares a source-linked agenda from the {DOCS}; structured decision fields generate approved instructions and proposed actions through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Departments used different measures and reported progress in incompatible formats. Direction and coaching could not be reduced to reporting rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and action-management features cover much of the work. Bounded extraction can organise narrative reports without delegating management decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting incentives, weak measures and sensitive conversations remain. Individual performance monitoring or trait-based allocation needs separate GDPR, EU AI Act and national consultation assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Judge competing needs, challenge misleading explanations and build trust with department leads.

ambition.what: A weekly cross-department capacity decision before service backlogs become escalations.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting status and more time coaching leads and resolving dependencies. They can gain authority to rebalance department capacity within an agreed operating envelope.

reach.task: Choose the operating model and level of shared services.
reach.learn: Service economics, organisational design and measures that reveal cross-department trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Dashboard summarisation and report questions are available today, subject to data-model quality.
Structured management-paper drafting is an existing capability; it supports preparation rather than managerial authority.
Trait-based task allocation and staff performance monitoring appear among high-risk employment uses under the EU AI Act.
Shared action records can remove duplicate status chasing when updates are maintained at source.

assumptions: Shares and remaining time are design estimates, not customer measurements.
Existing department metrics can be configured into a shared scorecard without rebuilding their source systems.
Action creation uses human-selected owners and deadlines.
Build ranges include access review and an initial consultation cycle where applicable; national procedures can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which measures department leads trust and which require manual adjustment.
Whether action status is maintained reliably in the existing {PROJECT}.
Existing delegation limits and escalation thresholds.
Whether the proposed reporting changes constitute employee monitoring under applicable national rules.
research_questions: Which reported measures encourage local optimisation at the expense of other departments?
Can structured decision capture replace narrative instructions without losing important qualifications?
new_work: Maintain measure definitions and escalation thresholds.
Review extracted issues and check missing or conflicting reports.
Keep action records current and investigate stale updates.
Review access rights and reassess employee-data use when reporting changes.
tasks.statement: Direct non-merchandising departments of businesses, such as advertising or purchasing.

tasks.short: Recommend facility locations and oversee renovations, balancing capacity, cost, disruption, and operational needs.

steps.what: Agree capacity needs, operational requirements, budget limits, and acceptable disruption.
Gather current occupancy, operating costs, staffing totals, and throughput records.
Inspect candidate premises or renovation areas with operational and technical specialists.
Review emailed designs, quotations, exclusions, and supplier delivery constraints.

loop.input: Supplier proposals, including quotations, layout descriptions, exclusions, and delivery terms.
loop.output: Offer notes with comparable fields, source passages, and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate amounts, currencies, dates, and totals deterministically. Reviewer confirms exclusions and scope comparability.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per proposal; unreadable or conflicting passages go to the facilities manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier formats and scope descriptions vary. Structured submissions use direct field mapping where available.

steps.what: Compare options for total cost, capacity, timing, disruption, and operational risk.
Write the recommended option, supporting assumptions, alternatives, and proposed delivery approach.

loop.input: Reviewed option appraisal, source evidence, and the operations manager's chosen recommendation.
loop.output: Investment recommendation covering costs, assumptions, alternatives, disruption, and unresolved risks.
loop.check: Insert figures directly from the appraisal. Require source references and manager review of every substantive claim.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims remain marked for human completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies the structure, but each site's trade-offs need a short narrative.

steps.what: Approve, reject, or request changes to the proposed investment.
Approve supplier awards and contractual commitments within delegated authority.
Coordinate contractors and department heads around access, sequencing, disruption, and emerging problems.
Record milestones, spending, open defects, and follow-up actions.
Inspect completed works and accept handover subject to specialist sign-offs and outstanding defects.

tasks.design: Configure a facility project template in the {PROJECT}, with approval records and links to evidence in the {DOCS}; a small integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins aggregate staffing, throughput, and costs from the {HCM}, {OPS_SYSTEM}, and {ERP}. A deterministic appraisal calculates comparable costs and scenarios, while bounded model loops extract proposal terms and draft the manager's recommendation. People retain site inspections, investment decisions, supplier commitments, coordination, and handover acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Projects are infrequent, proposals differ, and site knowledge sits with several specialists. Connecting operational records and maintaining a reusable appraisal often cost more than preparing another bespoke workbook.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, validation, and appraisal templates. Bounded extraction and drafting can handle variable proposal text; neither requires a new capability breakthrough.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden building defects, permit dependencies, contractual exclusions, and disruption estimates need specialist judgement. Use aggregate staffing data under GDPR; employee consultation and approvals depend on national rules and the proposed workplace changes.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether a site will work in practice, negotiating workable compromises, and accepting responsibility for capital and operational consequences.

ambition.what: Quarterly facility capacity and lease-option review.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into assembling comparisons and writing papers; more goes into site feasibility and resolving operational trade-offs. Investment and contractual decision rights remain within existing delegations.

reach.task: Compare the facility investment with other capital priorities.
reach.learn: Discounted cash flow, downside scenarios, capital constraints, and investment approval thresholds.

evidence.claim: A reusable appraisal, record integration, and configured project workflow are plausible deterministic building blocks; estimates require customer validation.
Board Intelligence Report Writer drafts structured papers from management documents. This supports the recommendation-drafting component, not facility selection.
Copilot in Power BI summarises reports and answers data questions. The digest warns that unprepared data models give inaccurate answers.
Physical inspections, technical acceptance, and capital trade-offs remain human work; the digest provides no documented facility-project automation case.

assumptions: Steps describe a representative project; location selection and renovation share an appraisal and delivery process but need different technical evidence.
Time shares cover the end-to-end task across participating roles and repeated coordination cycles, not only the operations manager's desk time.
Meetings and site visits take 54% of today's time, consistent with the supplied prior that judgement and coordination dominate.
A viable {PROJECT} configuration exists; building a replacement records application is unnecessary.
Qualified specialists supply technical assessments, permits, and completion certificates.
Remaining-time percentages and build-day ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Consent and access estimates include employee consultation where applicable; formal national processes may take longer and can overlap other work.
unknowns: Which facility decision is next, and whether selection, renovation, or both are in scope.
Available interfaces, data quality, and rights to use staffing, cost, occupancy, and throughput records.
Whether existing {PROJECT} templates and {ERP} connections can be configured directly.
Who approves investment, supplier commitments, scope changes, and handover at each value threshold.
Applicable national consultation, permitting, and workplace requirements.
Whether supplier proposals contain usable text and comparable scope.
Current project volumes, baseline effort, and enough reuse to justify ongoing upkeep.
research_questions: Which structured proposal fields capture the most consequential omissions across facility projects?
Which appraisal assumptions most often explain differences between approved budgets and completed-project costs?
Can existing {PROJECT} configuration support the required approvals and evidence links without custom development?
new_work: Check extracted proposal exclusions, assumptions, and scope differences.
Review generated recommendations and resolve unsupported claims.
Maintain cost mappings, appraisal formulas, approval thresholds, and project templates.
Handle failed imports, stale records, and missing specialist evidence.
Compare completed-project costs and disruption with the original appraisal.
tasks.statement: Recommend locations for new facilities, or oversee the remodeling or renovating of current facilities.

tasks.short: Plan store layouts and displays, test them on site and approve practical changes.

steps.what: Walk the store, measure constraints and observe customer movement.
Gather category sales, stock requirements and fixture specifications.
Sketch options and arrange sample fixtures or display materials on site.
Produce scaled plans in layout-design software.
Walk through a physical trial with store staff and identify necessary changes.
Approve layout, installation spending and disruption arrangements.
Send approved drawings and installation instructions to the delivery team.
Inspect the installed layout and decide whether further changes are needed.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator combines measured constraints, fixture dimensions and reusable layout patterns, using sales and stock extracts from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. The {OTHER} layout-design software exports scaled plans, while the {WORKFLOW} issues installation packs from the {DOCS} only after approval of the exact version and recipients.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurements and fixture data were often incomplete, while judgement depended on seeing the space. Bespoke layout generation was expensive relative to occasional redesign work.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable constraint checks and plan templates are cheaper to build and adapt. Existing drawing exports can remove redrawing and distribution work without requiring a model.
tasks.still_hard: Sightlines, customer behaviour, aesthetics and physical installation still need site trials. Accessibility, fire safety and other national rules require competent review; geometric checks alone cannot certify a layout.
tasks.human_edge: Notice how the store feels, anticipate staff and customer movement and judge whether a display serves the commercial aim.

ambition.what: A monthly small-zone layout trial with a defined commercial aim and rollback plan.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time gathering specifications and redrawing plans, while site judgement remains central. They can gain authority to approve small reversible trials within agreed spending and safety limits.

reach.task: Choose which store-format changes merit wider investment.
reach.learn: Retail space economics, trial design and how seasonality affects comparisons between layouts.

evidence.claim: Parameterized drawing, geometric constraint checks and template-based layout options can use deterministic software.
Physical trials remain necessary to assess visibility, movement, usability and practical installation.
The supplied digest contains no direct product evidence or documented case for store-layout automation.

assumptions: This task applies to a manager responsible for physical retail locations.
Shares describe a site-led redesign cycle and deliberately retain substantial physical work.
The existing {OTHER} layout-design software supports reusable fixture definitions and scaled export.
Initial scope covers one store format and a limited fixture catalogue.
Aggregate sales and manual observation suffice; access review covers GDPR, intended model use under the EU AI Act and any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Whether accurate measured plans and fixture dimensions exist.
Which import, export and template features the existing layout-design software supports.
Applicable national accessibility, fire-safety and employee consultation requirements.
Who can approve layout changes and external installation instructions.
Whether sales data can support useful before-and-after comparisons.
research_questions: Which reusable layout patterns produce useful options without excessive manual adjustment?
Which checks can be encoded reliably, and which need a site specialist?
How can a small-zone trial separate layout effects from promotions and seasonal demand?
new_work: Maintain measured plans, fixture dimensions and approved layout patterns.
Review generated options and investigate constraint conflicts.
Control drawing versions and installation recipients.
Record trial conditions, acceptance findings and rollback decisions.
tasks.statement: Plan store layouts or design displays.

tasks.short: Oversee site sustainability programmes, choose improvements and verify delivery and environmental results.

steps.what: Request site records and collect supplier evidence.
Consolidate site measures and resolve inconsistent units or missing evidence.

loop.input: Supplier invoices, waste tickets and meter records in the site evidence pack.
loop.output: Source-linked quantities, units, reporting periods and evidence exceptions.
loop.check: Require page references; apply deterministic unit conversions, duplicate checks and period checks.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; missing or ambiguous quantities go to the coordinator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents vary in layout and wording; structured feeds use deterministic parsing instead.

steps.what: Inspect site practices and discuss practical problems with local supervisors.
Choose improvement priorities, responsibilities and spending.
Write the programme plan, site instructions and proposed milestones.

loop.input: Approved priorities, budget, site findings and existing procedures.
loop.output: Draft programme with owners, milestones, site instructions and evidence requirements.
loop.check: Check budget totals and required fields; link instructions to approved priorities and supplied procedures.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved safety or regulatory questions remain explicit.
loop.why_not_simpler: Site-specific instructions require contextual writing; dates, costs and owners use fixed fields.

steps.what: Agree site implementation and supplier commitments.
Check programme milestones and environmental measures against targets.
Prepare and approve an internal programme progress report.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} collects site evidence into the {DOCS}, while a bounded extraction loop and deterministic checks build a traceable baseline on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. The {PROJECT} and {BI} track approved actions and targets; a bounded drafting loop prepares site plans, and a template generator produces internal progress reports from verified measures.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence arrived in inconsistent supplier documents and site questionnaires. Physical practices, ownership and measurement definitions varied between locations.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured intake, document extraction and evidence-linked records reduce collection work. Most tracking and reporting can use ordinary rules once measurement definitions are agreed.
tasks.still_hard: Physical verification, supplier reliability and selecting worthwhile changes remain demanding. Applicable environmental obligations, public claims and any CSRD reporting scope require specialist review.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise whether site practices actually changed, negotiate workable improvements and challenge attractive but weak environmental claims.

ambition.what: A quarterly cross-site waste-reduction clinic using verified cost and waste evidence.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling evidence and more time visiting sites and removing implementation barriers. They can gain authority to fund small site experiments within an approved programme budget.

reach.task: Prioritise environmental capital investment across locations.
reach.learn: Environmental measurement boundaries, investment appraisal and how to assess evidence behind sustainability claims.

evidence.claim: Sustainability reporting software can link evidence to datapoints and suggest reporting answers.
That reporting capability does not demonstrate automated site implementation or environmental improvement.
Document extraction, unit conversion and milestone tracking can support programme oversight with human exception handling.

assumptions: Shares include delegated evidence collection and programme preparation; all timings are illustrative.
The programme addresses operational improvement whether or not statutory sustainability reporting applies.
A sustainability coordinator and facilities lead support the manager.
Build ranges cover a small initial group of sites with agreed measurement definitions.
GDPR and EU AI Act checks apply to actual data and model use; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which environmental permits, reporting duties and CSRD requirements apply to the organisation.
Site count, evidence quality and supplier access arrangements.
Whether measures use consistent boundaries, units and reporting periods.
Who can approve site changes and supplier commitments.
Whether changed procedures require employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which evidence types account for most extraction errors and manual reconciliation?
Which proposed measures distinguish real improvement from changes in production volume or site boundaries?
new_work: Review ambiguous documents and missing evidence.
Maintain measurement definitions, conversion rules and evidence links.
Verify that programme actions changed physical practices.
Review generated instructions and investigate target exceptions.
Update programme templates when obligations or site procedures change.
tasks.statement: Implement or oversee environmental management or sustainability programs addressing issues such as recycling, conservation, or waste management.

tasks.short: Review financial and operational performance and choose improvement priorities.

steps.what: Retrieve financial statements, sales results and operational performance reports.
Align reporting periods, reconcile totals and calculate comparable performance measures.
Read departmental explanations and assemble the main variances and unanswered questions.

loop.input: Reconciled performance table and departmental reports with source identifiers.
loop.output: Variance brief separating measured changes, reported explanations and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Check every number against the table and every explanation against a cited passage; manager reviews.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per reporting period; unresolved claims become questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but departmental explanations contain varied free text.

steps.what: Challenge explanations with department heads and distinguish causes from reporting noise.
Approve improvement priorities, owners and investigation limits.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile {ERP}, {CRM} and {OPS_SYSTEM} data and feed a governed {BI} dashboard. A bounded model drafts a source-linked variance brief in {DOCS}; the manager challenges causes and approves priorities recorded in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reporting periods, metric definitions and departmental narratives differ. Existing reporting features often stop at departmental boundaries.
tasks.enabler_now: Established data connectors and calculation rules handle preparation. AI-assisted coding reduces bespoke integration effort, while a bounded model handles written explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Causal interpretation, cost allocation and incomplete operational data remain difficult. Employee-level measures require GDPR controls and an EU AI Act assessment if used for AI-based performance monitoring.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a favourable metric hides service damage, deferred maintenance or an unsustainable workload.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one operational improvement experiment.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling reports towards testing explanations and following improvement experiments. Formal spending and staffing authority does not expand automatically.

reach.task: Recommend which operational improvement deserves company investment.
reach.learn: Compare cash impact, strategic fit and opportunity cost across departments.

evidence.claim: Report summaries and data questions are available today; reliable answers depend on prepared data models.
Planning tools can draft narratives about assumptions and risks.
The digest reports a vendor case of reduced executive reporting effort, without a published measurement method.
Automating preparation does not establish the causes of performance changes or select worthwhile interventions.
AI-based staff performance monitoring is a listed high-risk use.

The manager reviews departmental performance rather than preparing the financial accounts.

Check whether selected experiments improved outcomes.
Monitor access permissions and model drafting errors.
tasks.statement: Review financial statements, sales or activity reports, or other performance data to measure productivity or goal achievement or to identify areas needing cost reduction or program improvement.

tasks.short: Direct administrative work supporting product delivery and service provision.

steps.what: Review pending order paperwork, service documentation and administrative backlogs.
Read escalations and identify missing documents, dependencies and requested decisions.

loop.input: Escalation message, linked request and permitted supporting documents.
loop.output: Exception brief with request identifier, missing items, dependencies and source passages.
loop.check: Validate identifiers and document existence deterministically; manager checks ambiguous interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per message; incomplete or conflicting cases enter manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Escalations describe missing paperwork and dependencies in inconsistent free text; structured requests bypass the loop.

steps.what: Allocate routine administrative requests to responsible teams.
Resolve competing priorities and approve exceptional administrative arrangements.
Copy decisions into a separate administrative tracking register.
Request completion updates and escalate overdue paperwork.

tasks.design: Configure one administrative queue in {WORKFLOW}, linked to records in {ERP}, {OPS_SYSTEM} and {HELPDESK}, with ownership and deadlines visible in {PROJECT}. A bounded extraction loop prepares briefs from unstructured {EMAIL} escalations; the manager approves exceptions, while routine routing and reminders follow configured rules. The shared decision record replaces the duplicate {SPREADSHEET} register.
tasks.previous_blocker: Administrative requests cross departmental systems, and exceptions arrive in messages. A separate register compensates for missing shared ownership.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured queues, forms and reminders cover routine work. Lightweight integrations and bounded text extraction connect the remaining gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Exceptions can require service, finance or contractual judgement. GDPR access restrictions must follow the underlying records, including attachments and extracted briefs.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently small paperwork exception creates a customer, contractual or operational problem.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time resolving recurring handoff failures with administrative supervisors. No new formal decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Recommend a shared administrative service model across departments.
reach.learn: Assess service cost, accountability, control separation and transition effort.

evidence.claim: Rules-based queues, ownership records and reminders can support routine administrative coordination.
A bounded extraction loop can prepare exception briefs, but this digest contains no documented case for this exact workflow.
Removing a duplicate register is feasible when the shared workflow provides the required record and reporting.

assumptions: The representative workflow is order and service administration; sector-specific administration will differ.
Administrative supervisors manage routine execution.
A small separate {SPREADSHEET} register currently duplicates operational decisions.
Only rule-covered requests are routed automatically; ambiguous exceptions remain with the manager.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one administrative workflow.
unknowns: Which administrative workflows actually consume the manager's time?
Does a duplicate register exist, and what reporting or retention duties does it fulfil?
Which exception decisions require finance, legal or customer approval?
Can existing request queues support cross-department ownership?
What access controls and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which request types can use structured forms instead of text extraction?
Which existing system can hold the authoritative administrative decision record?
new_work: Review ambiguous extraction results and misrouted requests.
Maintain responsibility mappings and escalation deadlines.
Resolve missing documents and broken record links.
Review recurring exceptions for process changes.
tasks.statement: Direct administrative activities directly related to making products or providing services.

tasks.short: Prepare staff schedules and duty allocations with supervisors, resolving coverage conflicts.

steps.what: Gather demand, staff availability, approved absences and required qualifications.
Build a draft roster in the workforce scheduling system {OTHER}.
Assign specific duties to rostered staff in the workforce scheduling system {OTHER}.
Discuss coverage conflicts, staff preferences and cross-team support with supervisors.
Approve consolidated coverage, overtime and duty allocations in the workforce scheduling system {OTHER}.
Publish approved schedules and duty assignments through the workforce scheduling system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Connect availability from {HCM}, qualifications from {LMS} and demand from {OPS_SYSTEM} to the workforce scheduling system {OTHER}. Configure deterministic coverage, qualification, working-time and preference rules to draft rosters and duties, with unresolved conflicts shown explicitly. Supervisors resolve exceptions with the manager, whose approval releases the schedule for publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability, qualifications and demand are maintained separately. Scheduling rules and informal staffing arrangements are only partly recorded.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling modules can apply explicit constraints and approval workflows. AI-assisted coding makes missing data connections cheaper to build; no model is needed for routine allocation.
tasks.still_hard: National working-time rules, collective agreements, fairness and last-minute absences require local judgement. GDPR applies to staff data; adding AI-based task allocation or performance monitoring requires an EU AI Act assessment and applicable employee consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate unpopular cover changes, recognise fatigue and balance preferences that cannot all be satisfied.

ambition.what: A cross-team cover desk for short-notice staffing gaps.

tasks.altitude: Supervisors spend less time constructing rosters; the manager focuses on unresolved cover and overtime choices. The cover desk would need an explicit mandate before reallocating staff across departments.

reach.task: Recommend a cross-department workforce resilience policy.
reach.learn: Compare minimum cover, overtime cost, employee experience and service continuity.

evidence.claim: Rules-based scheduling and constraint checks can generate draft rosters without a language model.
AI-based task allocation using personal traits or behaviour and staff performance monitoring are listed high-risk uses.
GDPR Article 22 limits solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
In the Netherlands, works-council consent provisions cover relevant working-time and employee monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: Supervisors prepare departmental schedules; the general manager handles consolidated coverage and exceptions.
The workforce scheduling system {OTHER} supports configurable deterministic rostering and duty rules.
If that capability is absent, a deterministic solver would replace configuration and require a revised build estimate.
Approved availability is used without copying medical absence details.
Time shares describe the end-to-end scheduling task, including supervisors' preparation.
Build ranges cover an initial scheduling group; consultation effort is indicative and formal processes may take longer.
unknowns: Which scheduling capabilities and interfaces are already licensed?
Which national rules, collective agreements and employee representation arrangements apply?
Are qualification, availability and preference records reliable?
Who can approve overtime and cross-team deployment?
How frequently do schedules change after publication?
research_questions: Can the configured scheduler explain infeasible coverage and every rule violation?
Can a shadow rollout meet coverage rules while preserving an agreed distribution of unpopular shifts?
new_work: Maintain working-time, qualification and coverage constraints.
Review infeasible schedules and last-minute staffing exceptions.
Check overtime and unpopular-shift distribution.
Handle employee corrections and schedule objections.
Maintain data access, consultation records and integration checks.
tasks.statement: Prepare staff work schedules and assign specific duties.

tasks.short: Monitor supplier delivery, quality, service and spending, and agree corrective action.

steps.what: Collect supplier commitments, delivery results and spending records.
Reconcile supplier results against service targets and budget.
Read supplier explanations and departmental reports about service failures.

loop.input: Supplier explanations and service incident reports linked to a supplier scorecard.
loop.output: Source-linked issues, disputed claims and missing evidence.
loop.check: Require source passages; validate identifiers and figures against the scorecard. Treat explanations as claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one validation retry per report; route unsupported claims to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explanations vary in wording and structure; numeric thresholds cannot interpret them.

steps.what: Review operational impact and alternatives with department managers.
Discuss causes, recovery commitments and commercial remedies with the supplier.
Approve corrective action and any changes to spending or supplier commitments.
Record agreed actions, assign owners and chase due dates.

tasks.design: Join commitments from the {PROCUREMENT}, receipts from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and spending from the {ERP} into a supplier dashboard in the {BI}. A bounded reader prepares source-linked issue briefs, while the {WORKFLOW} records approved actions and sends internal reminders. People handle supplier discussions and approve changes to commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier identifiers, receipt dates and service definitions differ across records. Reconciling them costs more than building the chart.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and scheduled joins can support scorecards. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort, and bounded extraction can shorten report reading.
tasks.still_hard: Attributing failures, measuring service quality and negotiating remedies remain difficult, especially with disputed evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether poor results reflect supplier failure, internal disruption or an unrealistic contract, and preserve negotiating options.

ambition.what: Weekly recovery decisions for suppliers showing deteriorating service.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time reconciling reports and more time resolving service risks. Contract and spending authority still follows existing delegation limits.

reach.task: Assess critical supplier concentration and continuity exposure.
reach.learn: Combine operational dependency, switching time and financial exposure into investment choices.

evidence.claim: Report summaries and dashboard questions are available capabilities; reliable results require prepared data models.
Deterministic joins, scorecards and action reminders are a plausible supplier-monitoring design, not a documented deployment here.

assumptions: This describes recurring oversight through procurement and department managers, rather than daily purchasing.
The time split gives substantial weight to discussion and judgement; collection effort varies by supplier.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for one supplier segment using existing infrastructure.
unknowns: Whether supplier identifiers match across the available systems.
Which service measures, budgets and remedies are contractually agreed.
Available access, export rights and approval limits.
Whether personal data in incident reports requires additional access restrictions.
research_questions: Which measures predict disruption early enough to change an operational decision?
Can standard reporting and reminder configuration cover the first release?
new_work: Resolve unmatched suppliers and disputed receipts.
Review extracted claims against source reports.
Maintain service definitions, thresholds and integration mappings.
Check stale feeds and close completed supplier actions.
tasks.statement: Monitor suppliers to ensure that they efficiently and effectively provide needed goods or services within budgetary limits.

tasks.short: Coordinate budgets, funding and investment choices across departments.

steps.what: Collect actuals, commitments, cash forecasts and departmental funding requests.
Reconcile departmental figures and assemble budget scenarios.
Read the financial pack and identify questions about variances and funding.

loop.input: Validated budget scenarios and source-linked department explanations.
loop.output: Financial review brief with variances, uncertainties and questions.
loop.check: Calculate figures deterministically; require source references and manager review of interpretations.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved claims revert to source tables.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but interpreting free-text explanations needs a bounded language step.

steps.what: Negotiate priorities, funding trade-offs and efficiency measures with department managers.
Approve funding within delegated limits or decide escalated requests.
Record approved budget changes and cost-centre allocations.
Chase agreed efficiency actions and report overdue commitments.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} data and feeds controlled scenarios in {BI}. A bounded drafting loop prepares source-linked review briefs; managers negotiate and approve funding through {WORKFLOW}. Approved decisions update the {ERP} and create tracked actions in {PROJECT}; payments remain separate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different account mappings, emailed assumptions and unclear approval limits made reliable consolidation expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing budget workflows and deterministic integrations handle most preparation. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort; a bounded drafting loop handles narrative explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling definitions, forecasting uncertain demand and settling competing departmental claims remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Judge which constraints matter, challenge optimistic assumptions and secure commitments from managers.

ambition.what: Weekly decisions on small transfers between discretionary operating budgets.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling packs and more time testing funding choices. Weekly transfers become possible within an explicitly delegated limit; larger investment rights stay with authorised budget holders.

reach.task: Prepare a ranked portfolio of cross-department investment options.
reach.learn: Capital appraisal, liquidity constraints and how strategic priorities determine investment trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Deterministic reconciliation, scenario calculations and approval routing can automate much of the preparation.
Copilot in Power BI summarises reports and answers data questions; data-model quality constrains reliability.
Pigment reports major forecast and executive-reporting savings in vendor cases; these do not establish savings here.

assumptions: Time shares are illustrative estimates for a recurring departmental budget cycle.
Financial decisions remain human; most change concerns preparation, recording and follow-up.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot with reusable connectors, not replacement of the finance architecture.
Access estimates include confidentiality review and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Available interfaces, account mappings and quality of commitment data.
Who can approve budget transfers and investment requests.
Whether existing planning workflows can record approvals and write budgets.
Whether any employee-level data is needed.
research_questions: Which reconciliation differences require judgement rather than mapping rules?
Does the existing budget module support the required scenario and approval process?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation exceptions and stale source data.
Review narrative explanations against cited figures.
Maintain account mappings, scenario assumptions and approval limits.
Monitor failed writes and duplicate decision records.
tasks.statement: Direct or coordinate financial or budget activities to fund operations, maximize investments, or increase efficiency.

tasks.short: Develop departmental policies, goals and procedures with leaders and staff, then coordinate implementation.

steps.what: Collect existing policies, operational evidence and staff proposals.

loop.input: An approved collection of current policies, operational evidence and staff proposals.
loop.output: Source-linked evidence brief listing issues, existing requirements and conflicting proposals.
loop.check: Require a source location for each claim; verify document versions and review contradictions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unsupported claims are omitted and gaps listed.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text proposals and policy documents express overlapping or conflicting requirements.

steps.what: Agree goals, policy choices and practical constraints with leaders and staff.
Draft the policy, procedures, goal definitions and implementation responsibilities.

loop.input: Agreed direction, proposed goals, controlled template and source-linked evidence brief.
loop.output: Policy draft and implementation plan with unresolved choices explicitly marked.
loop.check: Compare every obligation, target and named responsibility with agreed inputs; verify cited sources.
loop.stop: One draft and two revision passes; unresolved policy choices return to the policy owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply structure, but expressing agreed choices as clear procedures requires language drafting.

steps.what: Review legal, personnel, financial and operational implications.
Approve the policy and goals after resolving material objections.
Publish the approved version and notify affected staff.
Track implementation actions and assemble evidence of adoption.

tasks.design: Use controlled templates and versioned sources in {DOCS}, with bounded loops preparing evidence briefs and policy drafts. A configured {WORKFLOW} routes specialist reviews and records approval of an exact version before publication in {DOCS}. The approved implementation plan creates actions in {PROJECT} and feeds an adoption view in {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy evidence and comments were dispersed across documents and meetings, while drafting required substantial manual synthesis.
tasks.enabler_now: Version control and approval workflows already handle publication. Bounded extraction and drafting can reduce synthesis work when sources and agreed decisions are explicit.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing legitimate goals, resolving conflicting interests and interpreting applicable law require responsible people. Completion records do not prove that a policy works in practice.
tasks.human_edge: Decide what the organisation should require and secure acceptance from the people who must implement it.

ambition.what: Quarterly decisions on whether departmental procedures should be revised using implementation evidence.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rewriting documents and more time testing whether procedures achieve their goals. They can sponsor evidence-based revisions; formal policy approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Recommend which departmental policy experiments should become organisation-wide standards.
reach.learn: Governance mandates, consultation duties and evaluation of policy outcomes across departments.

evidence.claim: Board Intelligence Report Writer drafts structured papers from management documents, supporting the feasibility of bounded document preparation.
The documented flawed government report illustrates why generated references must be checked before approval.
Version-controlled publication and approval routing can be configured without model judgement.

assumptions: The policy owner supplies authoritative sources and agreed choices; the model does not invent requirements.
Time shares are illustrative for a substantive departmental policy change.
Publication is limited to the exact approved version and audience.
Build ranges cover one policy family and include access review and consultation planning.
Employee consultation or works-council involvement follows applicable national rules; substantive negotiations may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Who has authority to approve each policy type.
Which national consultation requirements and collective agreements apply.
Whether the document store supports version-specific approval and publication.
Which evidence can measure adoption without creating unnecessary employee monitoring.
Whether policy changes require system changes beyond document publication.
research_questions: Which sources are authoritative when existing policies conflict?
Can the approval workflow prevent publication of a modified, unapproved version?
Which outcome measures distinguish practical improvement from administrative completion?
new_work: Verify source references and remove unsupported obligations.
Maintain templates, source ownership and review dates.
Resolve specialist objections and consultation outcomes.
Handle failed publication or distribution rules.
Assess whether implementation evidence justifies revising the policy.
tasks.statement: Establish or implement departmental policies, goals, objectives, or procedures in conjunction with board members, organization officials, or staff members.

tasks.short: Select staff, agree training and conduct performance evaluations with personnel support.

steps.what: For hiring, assemble applications, interview criteria and approved role requirements.
Interview candidates and discuss evidence against the role criteria.
Select a candidate and record the evidence and proposed terms.
Prepare and issue the offer using approved terms.
For training, compare role requirements with course and certification records.
Discuss development needs and agree learning priorities with the employee.
Enrol the employee in agreed courses and set completion reminders.
For evaluation, assemble agreed goals, employee submissions and previous review records.
Discuss performance evidence, context and development with the employee.
Write and approve the assessment, recording employee comments and agreed actions.

tasks.design: Configure packs and approval routes in the {ATS}, role-based training checks in the {LMS}, and review preparation in {TALENT}. Approved fields populate offer templates in {DOCS} for authorised release through {ESIGN}, while agreed learning plans create {LMS} enrolments. Interviews, development conversations, candidate selection and performance assessments remain human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate personnel systems and inconsistent templates left managers and personnel staff assembling records manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing personnel modules often cover these workflows. Configuration and small deterministic connectors can remove preparation work without introducing model-based evaluation.
tasks.still_hard: Fair selection, candid feedback and understanding personal context remain human work. GDPR, access controls and national employment and consultation rules constrain how records are used.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise potential, hear an employee's explanation and take responsibility for decisions affecting their working life.

ambition.what: Offer a structured development conversation to shift employees outside the annual review window.

tasks.altitude: The manager gains time for interviews and development conversations, with less personnel paperwork. Hiring, training-spend and assessment rights do not change automatically.

reach.task: Identify organisation-wide capability gaps for workforce planning.
reach.learn: Aggregate workforce planning, succession risks and privacy-preserving use of personnel information.

evidence.claim: Pack assembly, approved-field offer generation and course enrolment are suitable for existing software configuration.
GDPR Article 22 constrains solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
AI used for recruitment decisions or staff performance evaluation can fall within Annex III high-risk categories.

assumptions: These are three recurring branches: hiring, learning and evaluation, not one sequence for every employee.
Shares represent an illustrative mix of those branches across the manager's personnel work.
Training checks use explicit role requirements and completion records, not inferred personal traits.
No model ranks candidates, scores employees or recommends employment consequences.
Build ranges include access design, employee consultation and works-council involvement where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which personnel modules and template features are enabled.
The manager's actual hiring and assessment authority.
Applicable national rules, collective agreements and consultation arrangements.
Lawful bases, retention periods and access permissions for each personnel record.
How much work falls into hiring, learning and evaluation locally.
research_questions: Which preparation steps can existing personnel modules already perform?
Which proposed changes alter monitoring or personnel decision processes and therefore require consultation?
Can capability reporting use aggregated records without exposing individual assessments?
new_work: Maintain role requirements, approved templates and enrolment rules.
Resolve incomplete or conflicting personnel records.
Review offer details before release.
Audit access permissions and retention settings.
Handle employee corrections and challenges to recorded evidence.
tasks.statement: Perform personnel functions, such as selection, training, or evaluation.

tasks.short: Coordinate cross-department initiatives, including sales promotions, from proposal through launch and review.

steps.what: Define the initiative's objective, scope and success measures.
Gather departmental capacity, dependencies and objections from messages.

loop.input: Department responses linked to one initiative.
loop.output: Readiness brief listing constraints, dependencies, proposed owners and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link every item to its message; distinguish proposals from accepted commitments.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unclear commitments remain unresolved for discussion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text responses express qualifications and objections that fixed fields cannot reliably capture.

steps.what: Resolve dependencies and agree departmental commitments.
Translate agreed commitments into a schedule with owners and dependencies.
Approve promotional launch after reviewing content, stock, service capacity and spend.
Chase milestone updates and escalate missed dependencies.
Review commercial results and agree changes for the next initiative.

tasks.design: Configure initiative templates, dependency checks and reminders in {PROJECT}, with structured readiness responses in {WORKFLOW}. A bounded loop turns remaining {EMAIL} and {CHAT} responses into a source-linked brief, while {BI} supplies results for review. Managers settle commitments and the campaign owner approves each external launch in {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Commitments were scattered across messages, and project records did not reliably reflect what departments had agreed.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project workflows can handle schedules and reminders. Small integrations and bounded extraction can connect the remaining narrative responses.
tasks.still_hard: Capacity conflicts, disputed ownership and commercial timing require negotiation. A complete checklist cannot establish that a launch is wise.
tasks.human_edge: Build commitment between managers and recognise when an apparently ready initiative will strain customer service or operations.

ambition.what: A weekly cross-department launch-readiness clinic for initiative owners.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time chasing updates and more time resolving launch constraints. They can recommend resequencing initiatives using shared capacity evidence; launch and spending rights remain explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Recommend which competing initiatives should receive scarce cross-department capacity.
reach.learn: Portfolio prioritisation, contribution margins and organisation-wide capacity trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Project templates, dependency rules and scheduled reminders can handle routine coordination.
The cross-government trial reported drafting savings but variable benefits; it does not establish initiative-coordination savings.
Source-linked extraction can prepare discussions without treating an inferred commitment as an accepted one.

assumptions: The steps illustrate a sales promotion; other initiatives use the same coordination pattern.
Time shares preserve the substantial human work in planning and agreement.
Build ranges cover one initiative template and a small set of connected systems.
Access work includes checking national consultation requirements if individual work tracking changes.
unknowns: Which role owns launch approval and which readiness checks are mandatory.
Whether departments maintain current capacity and milestone records.
Available project and campaign interfaces.
Whether reminders would introduce new employee monitoring.
research_questions: Which readiness questions can move from messages into existing structured forms?
Which dependency failures recur often enough for deterministic escalation?
new_work: Check extracted constraints and proposed commitments.
Maintain initiative templates and escalation thresholds.
Resolve contradictory updates and stale milestones.
Review whether reminders create noise or encourage superficial status reporting.
tasks.statement: Plan or direct activities, such as sales promotions, that require coordination with other department managers.

tasks.short: Set prices and business customer credit terms using demand forecasts, costs, payment history and commercial judgement.

steps.what: Gather demand forecasts, costs, sales results and customer payment history.
Calculate margin, volume and cash effects under alternative prices and credit terms.
Discuss demand assumptions, customer context and exposure with finance and sales managers.
Approve prices within delegated margin and discount limits.
Approve credit limits and payment terms within financial delegation.
Enter approved prices and terms with their scope and effective dates.

tasks.design: Join the {ERP} and {CRM} data on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, then calculate versioned margin, demand and cash scenarios for a {BI} view. Configure approvals in the {WORKFLOW} and transfer approved prices and credit terms into the {ERP} and {CRM}, checking scope, effective dates and delegation limits. The first version needs no model loop.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs, customer terms and forecasts use different definitions and update cycles. Approval decisions often arrive separately from the records that implement them.
tasks.enabler_now: Conventional scenario calculations, versioned datasets and existing approval functions can connect analysis to controlled record updates.
tasks.still_hard: Demand response is uncertain, payment history can mislead, and commercial exceptions may matter more than the calculated optimum.
tasks.human_edge: Choose acceptable margin and credit exposure while judging customer relationships, competitive response and uncertainty.

ambition.what: Weekly price reviews for product groups with rapidly changing input costs.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding scenarios and can revisit pricing assumptions sooner. Pricing authority stays within delegation, and finance retains credit approval.

reach.task: Set portfolio margin and working-capital priorities.
reach.learn: Assess price elasticity, cash conversion and concentration risk across business lines.

evidence.claim: Planning software can produce reports and flag anomalies; this supports analysis rather than autonomous commercial approval.
Deterministic scenario calculations and controlled updates are a plausible first implementation for this task.
GDPR Article 22 limits certain solely automated decisions concerning individuals.
The AI Act lists AI systems used to evaluate natural-person creditworthiness among high-risk uses.

assumptions: The initial scope is business customer accounts; natural-person credit scoring is excluded.
Pricing and credit approvals are separate and follow existing delegation.
Forecast scenarios expose uncertainty rather than claiming a known causal demand response.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for one business line with existing systems.
unknowns: Actual pricing and credit decision rights.
Whether accounts include sole traders or other natural persons.
Availability of historical price changes, lost sales and comparable demand observations.
Existing approval configuration and write access to commercial records.
Treatment of negotiated contracts, taxes, currencies and retrospective changes.
research_questions: Which demand assumptions can be tested against historical price changes?
Can existing commercial rules and approval configuration cover record activation?
Would any proposed expansion introduce natural-person decisions requiring additional GDPR and EU AI Act assessment?
new_work: Maintain cost definitions, approval limits and scenario assumptions.
Investigate missing prices, conflicting terms and stale forecasts.
Compare realised margin and payment outcomes with approved assumptions.
Review rejected updates and verify effective dates.
tasks.statement: Set prices or credit terms for goods or services, based on forecasts of customer demand.

tasks.short: Coordinate inbound, internal and outbound goods flows through supervisors, resolving capacity and service trade-offs.

steps.what: Review expected receipts, stock, production requirements and dispatch commitments.
Confirm actual constraints with production, warehouse and transport supervisors.
Compare feasible movement plans and their service, cost and sustainability effects.
Choose priorities and approve changes to movement plans.
Update movement schedules and issue instructions to warehouse and production teams.
Agree changed delivery or collection arrangements with carriers and suppliers.
Check execution and escalate unresolved delays or unsafe conditions.

tasks.design: Configure exception views in the {OPS_SYSTEM} and add a deterministic scenario calculator where existing planning functions fall short. The {WORKFLOW} transfers approved movement plans into schedules and internal instructions, with version and capacity checks. Managers and supervisors confirm physical constraints and direct interventions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recorded stock and capacity often lag physical conditions. Local constraints and external transport commitments are difficult to represent consistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing operational events, configurable alerts and conventional constraint calculations can improve preparation without a model loop.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded congestion, damaged goods, equipment failures and safety judgements require people close to the operation.
tasks.human_edge: Balance production continuity, customer promises, safety and practical site knowledge when no option satisfies every constraint.

ambition.what: Same-shift recovery decisions for emerging bottlenecks.

tasks.altitude: The manager receives earlier exception signals and compares feasible responses faster. Supervisors retain physical execution and safety authority; no new personnel decision rights are implied.

reach.learn: Translate recurring bottlenecks into capital needs, resilience benefits and investment payback.

evidence.claim: Operational alerts, constraint calculations and approved schedule updates can use deterministic technology.
The digest provides no documented case establishing automated physical goods-flow management for this setting.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to a company operating production or distribution facilities.
The manager coordinates through supervisors rather than routinely dispatching individual workers.
The workflow id 'other' denotes physical goods flow, which has no dedicated id in the supplied list.
The design changes goods schedules, not machinery controls or individual staff allocation.
Build ranges cover one site; access and consultation include national rules where changes affect working arrangements.
unknowns: Which operational planning, alerting and schedule-update features are already licensed.
Accuracy and latency of stock, capacity and equipment records.
Which movement changes require transport, safety or spending approval.
Applicable national consultation requirements and employee-representation arrangements.
Availability of reliable transport and emissions factors.
research_questions: Which constraints explain most failed movement plans?
Can existing planning configuration produce useful options before custom calculations are needed?
How should proposed schedules be tested against actual site conditions before rollout?
new_work: Maintain capacity constraints and transport factors.
Investigate stale operational events and false alerts.
Check approved plan versions before schedule updates.
Review recurring overrides with site supervisors.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
